```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "350px",
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
# needs ggcpb (figures) and cbsodataR (StatLine); without them nothing runs
run <- requireNamespace("ggcpb", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("cbsodataR", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = run)
if (run) source("quality-helpers.R")
```

> **How fast is the Dutch car fleet electrifying, and how does that differ by
> vehicle age, kilometres driven and region?**

The analysis itself will run in CBS Remote Access. This page develops its
code on simulated RDW files (`RDWNPACT`, `VERKEERSPRESTATIE`) and woonbase,
and uses StatLine to show which simulated results look like the real ones and
which will change when you switch to the real data. Similar pages:
`vignette("quality-income")` and `vignette("quality-energy")`.

## At a glance

::: {.glance}
| Result | Looks like reality? | In Remote Access |
|--------------------|----------|--------------|
| Cars per inhabitant, fuel mix, age profile | yes | similar; a large gap means a bug |
| Average annual kilometres | yes | similar, once weighted with `VPGEWICHT` |
| Car density per gemeente | ranking only | wider spread; company cars have no gemeente there either |
| Weight distribution | mean and spread only | different shape |
| EV share by construction year | no | concentrated in recent years |
| Kilometres by fuel | no | diesel much higher |
| Car ownership by income | no | falls steeply with income |
:::

Fuel, construction year, weight and mileage are drawn independently, so only
results that depend on one of them at a time look realistic. The code runs
unchanged either way; don't tune thresholds, classes or figure scales to the
simulated cross-tabulations.

## Simulated data

One woonbase population and RDW fleet per year, keeping active passenger
cars. `RDWNPACT` also holds dropped and business-stock vehicles, so filter on
the code for *active* passenger cars, not on the word "personenauto".

```{r simulate}
YEARS <- 2019:2025

simulate_year <- function(year) {
  sim_reset()
  woonbase_init(year = year, n = 20000L, seed = 42L)
  sim_init("rdw", year = year, seed = 43L)

  pers <- as.data.table(read_sav(sprintf("WoonbasePopulatiePersonen%dV1", year),
                                 col_select = c(RINPERSOON, GemeenteCodeJJJJ1Jan)))
  kent <- as.data.table(read_sav(sprintf("RDWNPACT%dTABV1", year),
    col_select = c(RINPERSOON, RINKENTEKEN, VRTGSOORT, BRANDSTCODECORVRTG,
                   EERSTETOELDAT1VRTG, MASSALEEGCORVRTG)))
  vp <- as.data.table(read_sav(sprintf("VERKEERSPRESTATIE%dTABV1", year),
                               col_select = c(RINKENTEKEN, VPJAARKM, VPGEWICHT)))

  kent[vp, on = "RINKENTEKEN", `:=`(jaarkm = as.numeric(i.VPJAARKM),
                                    vpgewicht = as.numeric(i.VPGEWICHT))]
  kent[, `:=`(year = year, n_pers = nrow(pers),
              bouwjaar = as.integer(EERSTETOELDAT1VRTG),
              gewicht = as.numeric(MASSALEEGCORVRTG),
              fuelcode = as.character(cbs_code(BRANDSTCODECORVRTG)))]
  kent[cbs_code(VRTGSOORT) == "6"]  # personenauto, actief park
}
cars <- rbindlist(lapply(YEARS, simulate_year))

# StatLine reports hybrids under petrol, so PHEV (A) and HEV (B) join petrol
cars[, brandstof := fcase(fuelcode %in% c("1", "A", "B"), "benzine",
                          fuelcode == "2", "diesel", fuelcode == "3", "lpg",
                          fuelcode == "4", "elektrisch", default = "overig")]
```

```{r statline, echo = FALSE}
sl_237 <- rbindlist(lapply(YEARS, function(y) {
  dt <- statline("85237NED", Perioden = period(y))
  if (!is.null(dt)) dt[, year := y]
  dt
}))
sl_236 <- statline("85236NED", Perioden = period(2023))
sl_404 <- statline("85404NED", Perioden = period(2023))
sl_pop <- statline("37230ned", Perioden = period(2023))
has_statline <- nrow(sl_237) > 0 && !is.null(sl_236) && !is.null(sl_404) &&
  !is.null(sl_pop)
```

```{r statline-note, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = run && !has_statline}
cat("> **Note.** StatLine could not be reached when this page was built, so",
    "only the simulated series are shown.\n")
```

StatLine tables used: 85237NED (fuel, construction year, weight), 85236NED
(vehicles by region), 85404NED (kilometres), 37230ned (population).

## Fleet size and fuel mix

```{r fleet}
sim_fleet <- cars[year == 2023, .N / n_pers[1] * 1000]
```

```{r fleet-table, echo = FALSE}
sl_fleet <- if (has_statline) {
  measure(sl_236[RegioS == "NL01"], "^Personenauto") /
    measure(sl_pop[RegioS == "NL01"], "^BevolkingAanHetBegin") * 1000
} else NA
knitr::kable(data.table(` ` = "Passenger cars per 1,000 inhabitants, 2023",
                        simulatie = round(sim_fleet), StatLine = round(sl_fleet)))
```

```{r fuel-mix}
sim_fuel <- cars[, .N, by = .(year, brandstof)][
  , .(brandstof, aandeel = N / sum(N) * 100, bron = "simulatie"), by = year]
```

```{r fuel-mix-plot, echo = FALSE, out.width = "700px"}
sl_fuel <- if (has_statline) {
  tot <- sl_237[grepl("^T", Bouwjaar)][, .SD[1], by = year]
  tot <- tot[, .(benzine = measure(.SD, "^Benzine"), diesel = measure(.SD, "^Diesel"),
                 lpg = measure(.SD, "^LPG"), elektrisch = measure(.SD, "^Elektriciteit"),
                 overig = measure(.SD, "^CNG") + measure(.SD, "^OverigOnbekend")),
             by = year]
  tot <- melt(tot, id.vars = "year", variable.name = "brandstof", value.name = "n")
  tot[, .(brandstof, aandeel = n / sum(n) * 100, bron = "StatLine"), by = year]
}
fuel <- rbindlist(list(sim_fuel, sl_fuel), use.names = TRUE)
fuel[, brandstof := factor(brandstof, levels = c("benzine", "diesel", "lpg",
                                                 "elektrisch", "overig"))]
p <- cpb_line(lines_bron(fuel[brandstof %in% c("benzine", "diesel", "elektrisch")]),
  x = year, y = aandeel, colour = bron, colour_index = c(6, 2), points = TRUE,
  facet = brandstof, facet_ncol = 3,
  title = "Brandstofmix personenauto's", ylab = "% van het wagenpark")
show_cpb(p, "fuel-mix", page = "full")
```

Both match up to sampling noise. Plug-in and regular hybrids are split from
petrol using fleet estimates, not a StatLine series, so questions about
hybrids specifically are less well grounded.

## Vehicle age

```{r age}
bin_bouwjaar <- function(y) {
  b <- pmin(2020L, pmax(2000L, y - y %% 5L))
  factor(fifelse(b == 2000L, "voor 2005",
                 fifelse(b == 2020L, "2020 en later", paste0(b, "-", b + 4L))),
         levels = c("voor 2005", "2005-2009", "2010-2014", "2015-2019", "2020 en later"))
}
cars23 <- cars[year == 2023, .(bouwjaargroep = bin_bouwjaar(bouwjaar), brandstof)]
sim_age <- cars23[, .(aandeel = .N / nrow(cars23) * 100,
                      aandeel_ev = mean(brandstof == "elektrisch") * 100,
                      bron = "simulatie"), by = bouwjaargroep]
```

```{r age-plot, echo = FALSE}
sl_age <- if (has_statline) {
  # single construction years only: the dimension also holds decade groups
  bj <- sl_237[year == 2023 & grepl("^Bouwjaar \\d{4}$", Bouwjaar_label)]
  bj[, `:=`(bouwjaargroep = bin_bouwjaar(as.integer(sub("Bouwjaar ", "", Bouwjaar_label))),
            elek = measure(.SD, "^Elektriciteit"),
            totaal = measure(.SD, "^Benzine") + measure(.SD, "^Diesel") +
                     measure(.SD, "^LPG") + measure(.SD, "^Elektriciteit") +
                     measure(.SD, "^CNG") + measure(.SD, "^OverigOnbekend"))]
  bj <- bj[, .(elek = sum(elek, na.rm = TRUE), totaal = sum(totaal, na.rm = TRUE)),
           by = bouwjaargroep]
  bj[, .(bouwjaargroep, aandeel = totaal / sum(totaal) * 100,
         aandeel_ev = elek / totaal * 100, bron = "StatLine")]
}
age <- rbindlist(list(sim_age, sl_age), use.names = TRUE)
p <- cpb_col(flip(age, "bouwjaargroep"), x = bouwjaargroep, y = aandeel, fill = bron,
  colour_index = c(2, 6), position = "dodge", orientation = "horizontal",
  title = "Personenauto's naar bouwjaar, 2023",
  ylab = "bouwjaar", xlab = "% van het wagenpark")
show_cpb(p, "age")
p <- cpb_col(flip(age, "bouwjaargroep"), x = bouwjaargroep, y = aandeel_ev, fill = bron,
  colour_index = c(2, 6), position = "dodge", orientation = "horizontal",
  title = "Elektrische auto's naar bouwjaar, 2023",
  ylab = "bouwjaar", xlab = "% elektrisch binnen bouwjaargroep")
show_cpb(p, "ev-by-age")
```

The age profile matches, because construction years are drawn from
85237NED. The EV share by construction year does not: in reality nearly all
electric cars are recent, while the simulator gives every construction year
the same EV share. The cross-tabulation code is fine; expect a completely
different picture in Remote Access.

## Kilometres and weight

```{r km}
cars23 <- cars[year == 2023 & !is.na(jaarkm)]
cars23[, groep := fcase(brandstof == "diesel", "diesel", brandstof == "lpg", "lpg",
                        default = "benzine/overige")]
# VPGEWICHT is about 1 in the simulation but not in the real file
sim_km <- rbindlist(list(
  cars23[, .(groep = "totaal", km = weighted.mean(jaarkm, vpgewicht))],
  cars23[, .(km = weighted.mean(jaarkm, vpgewicht)), by = groep]))[, bron := "simulatie"]
```

```{r km-plot, echo = FALSE}
sl_km <- if (has_statline) {
  sl_404[grepl("^Totaal", LeeftijdVoertuig_label) & grepl("^Totaal", Eigendomssituatie_label),
         .(groep = tolower(Brandstofsoort_label),
           km = measure(.SD, "^TotaalGemiddeldJaarkilometrage"), bron = "StatLine")]
}
km <- rbindlist(list(sim_km, sl_km), use.names = TRUE)
km[, groep := factor(groep, levels = c("totaal", "benzine/overige", "diesel", "lpg"))]
p <- cpb_col(km[!is.na(groep)], x = groep, y = km, fill = bron,
  position = "dodge", reverse_legend = FALSE,
  title = "Jaarkilometrage naar brandstof, 2023", ylab = "km per auto per jaar")
show_cpb(p, "km")

sl_wt <- if (has_statline) {
  tot23 <- sl_237[year == 2023 & grepl("^T", Bouwjaar)][1]
  n <- as.numeric(unlist(tot23[, grep("^k_\\d+Kg", names(tot23), value = TRUE), with = FALSE]))
  data.table(gewicht = c(400, seq(500, 2400, by = 100), 2500),
             aandeel = n / sum(n, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, bron = "StatLine")
}
sim_wt <- cars[year == 2023, .N,
               by = .(gewicht = c(400, seq(500, 2400, by = 100), 2500)[
                 cut(gewicht, c(-Inf, seq(450, 2450, by = 100), Inf), labels = FALSE)])][
  , .(gewicht, aandeel = N / sum(N) * 100, bron = "simulatie")]
p <- cpb_line(lines_bron(rbindlist(list(sim_wt, sl_wt), use.names = TRUE)),
  x = gewicht, y = aandeel, colour = bron, colour_index = c(6, 2), points = TRUE,
  title = "Personenauto's naar leeggewicht, 2023",
  ylab = "% van het wagenpark", xlab = "leeggewicht (kg, klassemidden)")
show_cpb(p, "weight")
```

The fleet-wide mileage matches, but diesel cars are driven much further than
petrol cars in reality and equally far in the simulator. Weight has the right
mean and spread, not the right shape, and does not differ by fuel.

## Region

```{r region}
sim_reset()
woonbase_init(year = 2023, n = 200000L, seed = 42L)  # enough persons per gemeente
sim_init("rdw", year = 2023, seed = 43L)

pers <- as.data.table(read_sav("WoonbasePopulatiePersonen2023V1",
                               col_select = c(RINPERSOON, GemeenteCodeJJJJ1Jan)))
kent <- as.data.table(read_sav("RDWNPACT2023TABV1", col_select = c(RINPERSOON, VRTGSOORT)))
kent <- kent[cbs_code(VRTGSOORT) == "6"]
kent[pers, on = "RINPERSOON", gemeente := as.character(i.GemeenteCodeJJJJ1Jan)]

sim_gem <- pers[, .(inwoners = .N), by = .(gemeente = as.character(GemeenteCodeJJJJ1Jan))]
sim_gem[kent[, .N, by = gemeente], on = "gemeente", autos := i.N]
sim_gem[, sim := fcoalesce(autos, 0L) / inwoners * 1000]
```

```{r region-plot, echo = FALSE}
if (has_statline) {
  sl_gem <- merge(
    sl_236[grepl("^GM", RegioS), .(gemeente = sub("^GM", "", RegioS),
                                   autos = measure(.SD, "^Personenauto"))],
    sl_pop[grepl("^GM", RegioS), .(gemeente = sub("^GM", "", RegioS),
                                   inwoners = measure(.SD, "^BevolkingAanHetBegin"))],
    by = "gemeente")
  gem <- merge(sim_gem[inwoners >= 500, .(gemeente, sim)],
               sl_gem[, .(gemeente, statline = autos / inwoners * 1000)], by = "gemeente")
  p <- cpb_scatter(gem, x = statline, y = sim,
    title = "Auto's per 1.000 inwoners per gemeente", ylab = "simulatie", xlab = "StatLine") +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed")
} else {
  p <- cpb_hist(sim_gem[inwoners >= 500], x = sim, bins = 30,
    title = "Auto's per 1.000 inwoners (simulatie)",
    ylab = "aantal gemeenten", xlab = "auto's per 1.000 inwoners")
}
show_cpb(p, "region")
```

The ranking of gemeenten is reproduced (correlation
`r if (run && has_statline) round(cor(gem$sim, gem$statline), 2) else "n/a"`). The
simulated densities are lower because company cars have no owner in the
population, while StatLine counts them at the company's address; the
outliers where lease companies are registered are missing for the same
reason.

## Income

```{r income}
hh <- as.data.table(read_sav("WOONBASEEKHuishoudensWV2023V1",
                             col_select = c(RINPERSOON, P100HBEST1JAN)))
hh_nr <- as.data.table(read_sav("WoonbasePopulatieHuishoudens2023V1",
                                col_select = c(RINPERSOON, HUISHOUDNR1Jan)))
pers_hh <- as.data.table(read_sav("WoonbasePopulatiePersonen2023V1",
                                  col_select = c(RINPERSOON, HUISHOUDNR1Jan)))
hh[hh_nr, on = "RINPERSOON", HUISHOUDNR1Jan := i.HUISHOUDNR1Jan]
kent[pers_hh, on = "RINPERSOON", HUISHOUDNR1Jan := i.HUISHOUDNR1Jan]
hh[, `:=`(heeft_auto = HUISHOUDNR1Jan %in% kent$HUISHOUDNR1Jan,
          deciel = factor(pmin(10L, ceiling(as.numeric(P100HBEST1JAN) / 10)), levels = 1:10))]
```

```{r income-plot, echo = FALSE}
p <- cpb_col(hh[!is.na(deciel), .(zonder_auto = mean(!heeft_auto) * 100), by = deciel],
  x = deciel, y = zonder_auto,
  title = "Huishoudens zonder auto (simulatie)",
  ylab = "% huishoudens", xlab = "deciel besteedbaar huishoudinkomen")
show_cpb(p, "income")
```

Car owners are drawn regardless of income, so the share of households
without a car is flat across income deciles, while in reality it falls
steeply with income. The join runs as on the real data; the result does not
look like it.

## Before you move to Remote Access

The simulated files already have the structure that trips up code on the real
data, so the code above handles it:

- **Vehicle status.** `RDWNPACT` holds dropped and business-stock cars; the
  filter on code 6 keeps active passenger cars only.
- **Several vehicles per owner.** Counts per person or household use `.N` and
  `%in%`, not one row per person.
- **Owners outside the population.** Company cars and owners not in the GBA
  (`RINPERSOONS` K or S) do not join to woonbase, so they are missing from
  the gemeente and income breakdowns, as they will be in Remote Access.
- **`VERKEERSPRESTATIE`** holds active passenger cars of natural persons
  only, and `VPGEWICHT` varies, so the kilometres are weighted.

What still differs is content, not structure: the combinations of fuel,
construction year, weight, mileage and income listed at the top.
